The Court made the following Common Judgment;
Challenge in the Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is to the Order, dated 25.10.2016, in M.V.O.P. No.164 of 2014 on the file of Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-l Additional District Judge, Srikakulam (for short, 'the Tribunal') whereunder'the Tribunal, dealing with a claim of compensation made by the claimants for Rs.4,00,000/-, on account of the death of Marpu Narasimha Murty (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased'}, in a motor vehicle accident,
which was occurred on 30.05.2013 af about 05:30 PM, in between Kattivaram colony and N.M.
Puram, Kanchili Mandalam, Srikakulam District, awarded a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation, with interest at the rate of 9% AVRB.J p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization against the respondent Nos.1 to 3.
The Tribunal apportioned the compensation as a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- to the first petitioner and Rs.50,000/- each to the second and third petitioners respectively.
The parties to this Appeal will hereinafter be referred to as O described before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. The case of the claimants, in brief, according to the averments set out in the claim, before the Tribunal, is that first petitioner is the wife and second and third petitioners are major sons of the deceased.
First respondent is the driver, second respondent is the owner and third respondent is the insurer of the Luggage Van bearing No.AP-30W-2275 (for short, 'the offending vehicle') with valid insurance.

On 30.05.2013 at about 03:00 PM the deceased engaged the offending vehicle of the second respondent at Binnala Madanapuram to go to Kattivaram village to unload the flour mill machinery at Kattivaram and accordingly they reached Kattivaram and unloaded the said machinery.

On return journey to his village, EJinnala Madanapuram, when the deceased reached the place of accident at about 05:30 PM, the first respondent driver of the offending vehicle, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, and was unable to control, as a result the offending vehicle turned turtle.
The deceased sustained injuries and immediately he was shifted to Community Health Centre, Sompeta in 108 ambulance and from there to KGH, Visakhapatnam.
The deceased, while undergoing treatment at KGH, Visakhapatnam, died on 09.06.2013 AVRB.J on account of the injuries received by him in the accident.

Originally, the Station House Officer, Kanchili Police Station registered a case against the first respondent in Crime No.61 of 2013 for the offences under Sections 337 and 338 IPC and, after receipt of death intimation of the deceased, section of law was altered to Section 304-A IPC.
Police filed charge sheet against the first respondent in C.C. No. 130 of 2013 before the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Sompeta.

5. Third respondent/insurer of the offending vehicle got filed a counter denying the averments of the petition and contending in substance that the claimants have to prove the manner of the accident,
age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The alleged accident took place while the petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle, which is a luggage van and meant to carry the goods alone.
The deceased traveled in the offending vehicle as an unauthorized passenger.
Hence, third respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
At the time of accident, more persons than the seating capacity of the vehicle were traveling in the offending AVRB.J vehicle.
There is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
The claim is excessive.
Hence, the claim is to be dismissed.

6. The Tribunal, on the basis of the aforesaid pleadings, settled the following issues for trial:
1.
Whether the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the first respondent-driver of van bearing Regn. No.AP 30 W 2275?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, as prayed for? If so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?
3.

relief

During the course of trial on behalf of the claimants before the r /.
Tribunal, PWs.1 and PW.2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-5 were marked.
Further, during the cross-examination of PW.2, certified copy of altered First Information Report was marked as Ex.B-1.
On behalf of the contesting third respondent, RW.1 was examined and E;x.B-2 - copy of insurance policy was marked.
Further, RW.2 Junior Assistant in RTO office was examined and Exs.X-1 to X-4 were marked.

8. The Tribunal, on hearing both sides and after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, answered the first issue against the driver of the offending vehicle and while deciding the second issue, the Tribunal arrived at the compensation of AVRB.J Rs.4,56,000/- but as the petitioners claimed the compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-, the Tribunal restricted the compensation amount to Rs.4,00,000/- as claimed by the petitioners.
9. The un-successful third respondent/insurer, feeling aggrieved of the aforesaid order, filed the present Appeal.

10. The claimants filed the Cross Objection in the present Appeal with a prayer to enhance the compensation on the ground that the age of the deceased was to be considered as 45 years and the proper multiplier should be 13 instead of 11 and further the Tribunal . was not justified in awarding Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144680793/

1.

Whether the Order of the Tribunal in M.V.O.P. No. 164 of 2014, dated 25.10.2016,
on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-l Additional District Judge, Srikakul^m is sustainable under law and AVRB.J facts and whether there are any grounds to reduce the compensation as contended on behalf of the appellant?

Sri V. Roopesh Kumar Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant/insurer, would contend that the Tribunal erroneously held that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, though the evidence on record did not prove the same.
The deceased was an un-authorized passenger travelling in the offending vehicle which the Tribunal failed to consider.
Apart from that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license.
Though the third respondent/appellant got examined RWs.1 and RW.2 in support of such contention, the Tribunal did not look into the same properly.
The compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is highly excessive.
He would further submit that there are no merits in the Cross-Objection filed by the claimants.
Claimants' themselves restricted their claim to Rs.4,00,000/- but the Tribunal arrived at F^s.4,56,000/- erroneously.
He would submit that the amount of compensation that was awarded is on higher lines, which needs to be reduced accordingly.
AVRB.J 13.

Sri Kolia Venkateswarlu, learned counsel for the respondents/cross-objectors, would contend that the evidence on record would prove the fact that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle wherein the deceased was traveling as owner of the goods.
Police concluded the investigation and laid charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The owner as well as the driver remained ex parte and did not choose to contest the claim.
The Tribunal rightly held that the accident occurred was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

He would submit that even if the age of 50 years as Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144680793/
6 evident from the claim of the claimants which was supported by post-mortem report is taken into consideration, the appropriate multiplier should be 13 but the Tribunal erroneously fixed the multiplier 11, applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years.

sentences.text: He would submit that the law is well settled that though the claimants did not pray for appropriate compensation , the same can be granted.

Having arrived at the findings that the claimants are entitled to Rs.4,56,000/-, the Tribunal was not justified in awarding only Rs.4,00,000/- on the ground that the claimants only prayed for the same.
The finding of fact recorded by the Tribunal was also that the deceased was self employed because he was running a flour mill.
The Tribunal ought to have considered the future prospects.

He would further submit that the petitioners claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.6,000/- p.m.
but the Tribunal erroneously fixed up the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- p.m.

His ultimate contention is that appropriate multiplier AVRB.J is 13 and the monthly income of the deceased is to be taken into consideration as Rs.6,000/- and further future prospects are also be awarded to the petitioners/cross-objectors because the deceased was self employed.

With the above submissions he would contend that the compensation needs to be enhanced considerably from F?s.4,00,000/- to Rs.6,00,000/-.
14.
As seen from the evidence of PW.1, wife of the deceased, she deposed in tune with her pleadings.
Through her examination E;xs.A-1 to A-5 were marked.
Admittedly, PW.1, wife of the deceased, was not a witness to the occurrence.
However, petitioners examined one D. Ramanamurthy, direct witness to the occurrence.
The evidence of PW.2 is that on the date of accident on 30.05.2013, the deceased engaged the offending vehicle to go to Kattivaram village to move his flour mill machinery.
He accompanied the deceased.
They unloaded the machinery at Kattivaram and they started to return to their village.

When the offending vehicle reached near the place of accident at about 05:30 PM, first respondent being driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in -a rash and negligent manner and unable to control the vehicle, as such the vehicle turned turtle.
The deceased sustained injuries in the accident.
He testified that the accident took place was due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the first respondent.
During the course of cross-examination, he denied the theory of contesting third respondent.
AVRB.J 15.

There is no dispute that pertaining to the incident in question, the Police registered FIR in Crime No.61 of 2013 of Kanchili Police Station and, after concluding investigation, they have filed charge sheet.
Those facts are evident from Exs.A-1 and A-2., certified copy of FIR and charge sheet.
Exs.A-4 and A-5, certified copy of postmortem report and inquest report proves the fact that cause of death of the deceased was due to multiple injuries received in the accident.
There were no mechanical defects in the offending vehicle as per Ex.A-3 - MVI report.
For obvious reasons, the driver of the offending vehicle remained ex parte.
There is no rebuttal evidence.
Though the third respondent examined RW.1 but he was only representative of the third respondent who deposed on the basis of the records.
The evidence of RW.2 is regarding the so called seating capacity of the offending vehicle.
So the direct witness - PW.2 supported the case of the claimants.
There was no rebuttal evidence.
It is a case where the Police conducted investigation as to the circumstances in which the deceased met with accident and they filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, the petitioners quietly proved before the Tribunal that the accident occurred was due to rash Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144680793/
7 ahd negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the first respondent.
16.

sentences.text: There is no dispute about the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
First petitioner is the wife, second and third petitioners are major sons of the deceased.
AVRB.J 17.
Turning to the age of the deceased, according to the contention of the claimants, the Tribunal erred in applying proper multiplier.
The case of the claimants is that the deceased was aged about 50 years.
As seen from Ex.A-4 - post-mortem report, deceased was shown as aged 50 years.
Though the petitioners did not file any date of birth certificate of the deceased but their case has support from Ex.A-4 - post-mortem report.
Now by virtue of the cross-objection, the contention of the claimants is that the deceased Vi/as aged about 45 years in view of the Aadhaar card.
It is to be rioted that the so called Aadhaar card cannot be taken as date of birth proof.
So, even if the contention of the claimants that the deceased was aged 50 years

is taken into consideration, the appropriate multiplier in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sar/a Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and others^ is 13 but not 11 as applied by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Sar/a Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and others^
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: What is evident from the order of the Tribunal is that, it took note of the fact that the claim of the petitioners was that the deceased was aged 50 years and that Ex.A-4 proves the same.

The Tribunal erroneously vi/ithout any basis was of the view that because the first petitioner vi/as aged 47 years and the second and third petitioners were aged 23 and 21 years, the age of the deceased is more than 50 years.
Those findings are nothing but irregular.
Hence, it is absolutely safe to consider the age of the deceased as 50 years as such appropriate multiplier for the age group of 46 to 50 years is 13.
The 2009 ACJ 1298 AVRB.J Tribunal erred in applying the multiplier 11 by erroneously looking into the age of the deceased in the age group of 51 to 55 years.
18. It is a case where the claim of the petitioners was that the deceased was running a flour mill and earning Rs.6,000/- pm.
So, according to the petitioners, the deceased was self employed, because he was running a flour mill.
They pleaded that the income of the deceased was Rs.6,000/- p.m.

Even according to Exs.A-1, A-2 and A-5, the deceased had a flour mill and accident was occurred when he was moving flour mill machinery in the offending vehicle of the second respondent to some other place.

The Tribunal considered the earnings of the deceased on notional theory as Rs.4,500/- p.m.
because there was no authentic proof to prove the income of the deceased.
It is to be noted that the flour mill machinery has been with the family members of the deceased and they can as well operate it.
However, the fact remained is that the deceased was personally looking after the flour mill machinery.
In the absence of the deceased, if the petitioners wanted to continue the same, definitely they need some person, who can supervise the operations of the flour mill.
Looking into the minimum wages which were in force around the year 2013 i.e., the accident year, income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- p.m. fixed by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable.
Hence, insofar as the act of the Tribunal in considering the income of the deceased as that of Rs.4,500/- is absolutely reasonable.
Supervisory expenses, which the petitioners have to incur to look after the flour mill in the absence of the deceased, is to be considered as loss of earnings to the claimants.
It.is to be noted AVRB.J

that, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others^, if the deceased is self employed or with permanent job or on a fixed Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144680793/

sentences.text: 8 salary, future prospects is to be awarded.
Here, it is quietly evident from the record that the deceased was self employed.

The observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (2"'^
supra) at Para No.61

are as follows:
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component".
19. Here, the age of the deceased was 50 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, an addition of 25%
is to be added to his income towards his future prospects.
As this Court already pointed out, the Tribunal considered the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- p.m.
So when Rs.4,500/- is multiplied with 12, it would come to F^s.54,000/- p.a.
If 25% of Rs.54,000/- i.e., Rs.13,500/- is added to Rs.54,000/-, it would come to Rs.67,500/-.

As the claimants are three in number, 1/3'^'^
of Rs.67,500/- which is Rs.22,500/- is to be deducted from Rs.67,500/- towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The net contribution vof the deceased to his family ^2017 ACJ 2700 AVRB.J members would be Rs.45,000/-.
As this Court already pointed out the appropriate multiplier for the age group of 46 to 50 years is 13, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (1* supra).
The multiplicand to be arrived at is Rs.45,000/- x 13 == Rs.5,85,000/-.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (2"^^ supra), the amount of compensation to be awarded under conventional heads i.e., for consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is Rs.40,000/- + Rs. 15,000/- Rs. 15,000/- respectively which amounts to Rs.70,000/- but the Tribunal under the aforesaid three heads awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/-.

So,
the total compensation which can be awarded to the claimants/cross-objectors is Rs.5,85,000/- +
Rs.70,000/-, which comes to Rs.6,55,000/-.

The petitioners/cross-objectors paid an amount of Rs.2,000/- towards court fee praying to enhance the compensation amount to Rs.6,00,000/- but the compensation to be awarded to them is crossing Rs.6,00,000/-.
They have to pay the proportionate deficit Court fee in the Registry on the compensation amount of Rs.55,000/-.

20. It is also the contention of the appellant/insurer that the Tribunal awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a. but in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (1* supra) is only 7.5%.

21. Turning to the aspect that against whom the responsibility is to be fixed to pay compensation,
the contention of the appellant/insurer is that the deceased was travelling in the offending AVRB.J vehicle as un-authorized passenger.
The contention deserves no merit.
The outcome of the investigation was also that while the deceased was shifting his flour mill machinery, the accident took place.
Hence,' such contention has no merit at all.
Apart from this, there is no dispute that as on the date of accident, there was an insurance policy covering the offending vehicle.

Though it was contended on behalf of the appellant that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle against the seating capacity but it is a case where RW.1 admitted that according to Ex.X-2, it did not disclose that one seat is meant for driver only.

RW.1 admitted in cross-examination that as per Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144680793/
9 Ex.B-2 - insurance policy, 1+1 coverage is available to the vehicle.

entities.text: Marpu Saraswari vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, it goes without saying that the seating capacity of the offending vehicle is 1+1 including the driver.

So, even according to Ex.B-2,
there is a seat for another person to travel along with the driver for which the owner of the vehicle paid the premium.

The Tribunal rightly pointed out that it is not the case of the third respondent/insurer that other persons who allegedly travelled along with the deceased in the accident van, filed petitions claiming compensation.
So, the Tribunal rightly held that there was space for the deceased to travel in the offending vehicle being owner of the goods.
22. Turning to the contention of the appellant that the first respondent has no valid driving license

,
it was borne out by the evidence of RWs.1 and RW.2 including Ex.X-4 - driving license that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving license to drive Light Motor Vehicle for non-transport J;?ut the fact is that he drove the AVRB.J transport vehicle.
The Tribunal rightly held that the skill to drive a transport vehicle and non-transport vehicle is the same.
The Tribunal with proper rulings rightly negated the contention of the appellant/insurer.
Under the circumstances, as rightly held by the Tribunal, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
23. In view of the above reasons, this Court is of the considered view that there are no merits in the grounds of Appeal as such insofar as the Appeal is concerned, it is to be dismissed.

Coming to the Cross Objection filed by the respondents/claimants, the compensation has to be enhanced from that of Rs.4,00,000/- to that of Rs.6,55,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

24. In the result, the Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed but under the circumstances without costs and the Cross Objection is allowed enhancing the compensation from Rs.4,00,000/- to that of Rs.6,55,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit by holding that the respondent Nos.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is a case where the Police conducted investigation as to the circumstances in which the deceased met with accident and they filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
So, even if the contention of the claimants that the deceased was aged 50 years
is taken into consideration, the appropriate multiplier in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sar/a Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and others^ is 13 but not 11 as applied by the Tribunal.
What is evident from the order of the Tribunal is that, it took note of the fact that the claim of the petitioners was that the deceased was aged 50 years and that Ex.A-4 proves the same.
The Tribunal erroneously vi/ithout any basis was of the view that because the first petitioner vi/as aged 47 years and the second and third petitioners were aged 23 and 21 years, the age of the deceased is more than 50 years.
Hence, it is absolutely safe to consider the age of the deceased as 50 years as such appropriate multiplier for the age group of 46 to 50 years is 13.
The 2009 ACJ 1298 AVRB.J Tribunal erred in applying the multiplier 11 by erroneously looking into the age of the deceased in the age group of 51 to 55 years.
Looking into the minimum wages which were in force around the year 2013 i.e., the accident year, income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- p.m. fixed by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable.
Hence, insofar as the act of the Tribunal in considering the income of the deceased as that of Rs.4,500/- is absolutely reasonable.
Supervisory expenses, which the petitioners have to incur to look after the flour mill in the absence of the deceased, is to be considered as loss of earnings to the claimants.
Apart from this, there is no dispute that as on the date of accident, there was an insurance policy covering the offending vehicle.
Though it was contended on behalf of the appellant that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle against the seating capacity but it is a case where RW.1 admitted that according to Ex.X-2, it did not disclose that one seat is meant for driver only.
So, it goes without saying that the seating capacity of the offending vehicle is 1+1 including the driver.
So, the Tribunal rightly held that there was space for the deceased to travel in the offending vehicle being owner of the goods.
,
it was borne out by the evidence of RWs.1 and RW.2 including Ex.X-4 - driving license that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid driving license to drive Light Motor Vehicle for non-transport J;?ut the fact is that he drove the AVRB.J transport vehicle.
The Tribunal rightly held that the skill to drive a transport vehicle and non-transport vehicle is the same.
Under the circumstances, as rightly held by the Tribunal, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
